info.name: ETL Console customer API v1.0.0-draft
info.description:
Start work, follow it, decide on it, and be told when something happens.

Get a token first (auth › the token request): it stores accessToken for every other request.

item.name: auth
Exchange the client's id and secret for an access token (15 minutes).

request.description:
Exchange the client's id and secret for an access token (15 minutes).

operationId: createToken

exec: // Keeps the token for the other requests (collection variable accessToken).

item.name: pipelines
The pipelines this client may start or read.

request.description:
The pipelines this client may start or read.

operationId: listPipelines

item.name: One pipeline, with its input contract and the event types its runs emit.

request.description:
One pipeline, with its input contract and the event types its runs emit.

operationId: getPipeline

item.name: runs
Start a run with a record and/or uploaded files (push intake).

header.description: Without format: application/json, application/pdf, text/html or text/markdown (by q, then order; */* is json). An Accept naming none of them is a 400 (unsupported-format). For POST /pipelines/{pipelineId}/runs only with wait.

query.description: Seconds to wait for the run to end, 1 to 60 (`30` or `30s`). Absent: answer at once (202).
json (the default), pdf, html or md. Wins over Accept. Anything else is a 400 (unsupported-format).
pdf, html and md of a run that made several reports: which one, by its number (RPT-0093).

request.description:
Start a run with a record and/or uploaded files (push intake).

The record is validated against the pipeline's input contract first; nothing is stored when it fails (422, each field's path under "record"). Every file id must be one of the workspace's own files (422 at "files[i]"). The record and the files are handed to the run as its intake: one JSON object with the record's fields and the start's own under names beginning with "_" (_reference, _files, _file_ids, _file_bucket, _file_key, ...). One run of a pipeline is in flight at a time (409 while one is). Sending the same Idempotency-Key again returns the first run. `parameters` are the run's parameter values by name, checked as the pipeline declares them (GET /pipelines/{id} lists them): a name it does not declare, a value of the wrong type or a required one with no value and no default is a 422 at "parameters.<name>", and nothing starts. Run and wait: with `wait` (1 to 60 seconds), the answer waits for the run to end -- ended in time, 200 with the run and its `result` (a completed run's final output, as GET /runs/{runId}/result gives it); still going, the 202 and its Location, as without `wait`. A replay with the same Idempotency-Key waits again for the same run. With `wait`, `format` (or the Accept header) chooses the waited answer's format, as GET /runs/{runId}/result's: json (the default, the Run and its result); pdf, html or md -- once the run ends, exactly what GET /runs/{runId}/result answers in that format (the document, or its problem: a run that did not complete is a 409 run-not-completed), always with the run's Location. An unsupported format is a 400 and nothing starts.

operationId: startRun

item.name: Runs, newest first.

request.description:
Runs, newest first.

Every run of the workspace's pipelines, however it started (the API, an event, the console, a schedule), newest first. The filters combine. updatedAfter compares the run's latest time (its end, else its start, else its creation); createdAfter its creation. Times are RFC 3339 with an offset; a filter that is not one is 400.

operationId: listRuns

item.name: One run, with its status, times (UTC) and review status.

request.description:
One run, with its status, times (UTC) and review status.

operationId: getRun

item.name: Retry a failed run from the step that failed, or from the start.

request.description:
Retry a failed run from the step that failed, or from the start.

Runs a failed run again as its next attempt (the same run id; `attempt` goes up by one). With no body, or `{"from": "failed_step"}`, it resumes from the first step of the latest attempt that did not complete: the steps before it are not run again -- their kept outputs are reused, and their work is not billed again -- and the step that failed and every step after it run, on the pipeline as it is now. `{"from": "start"}` runs every step again. A resume is refused (409, the problem's `type` says why) when the run is not failed (`run-not-failed`), another run of the pipeline is in flight (`run-in-flight`), the pipeline is inactive (`pipeline-inactive`) or its workspace paused (`workspace-paused`), the pipeline changed before the failed step (`pipeline-changed`: only the failed step and later steps may change; a step's name, retries, timeout and on-error may), a file a reused step read has changed since, judged by its sha256 (`input-changed`), a reused step's kept output has expired (`outputs-expired`: outputs are kept for the pipeline's retention, 24 hours unless set), or there is nothing to resume from (`not-resumable`: the run ran no steps, every step completed, or it has had 20 attempts). From the start, only the first four apply. Answered once the run is queued; follow it as any run, or by its `run.started` and `run.completed` or `run.failed` events, which carry the new `attempt` and `retry`.

operationId: retryRun

item.name: The run's steps in order (its latest attempt).

request.description:
The run's steps in order (its latest attempt).

The steps of the run's latest attempt, in order, with their status, rows in and out, and times. A run of a pipeline without steps is shown as its one step, key "legacy". A new kind of step appears here as it is, with its own task name: there is no endpoint per step kind.

operationId: listRunSteps

item.name: The run's manifest: the files it received and made, by file id, and its review.

request.description:
The run's manifest: the files it received and made, by file id, and its review.

The files the run's latest attempt made (role result, or report for a PDF) and, for a run started through the API, the files it was given (role input), each by its file id: GET /v1/files/{fileId} downloads it. A step that makes a PDF lists two files with the same step: the PDF (report), which prints the first rows of a big table, and the full data beside it as a CSV (result), unless the step turns that off. Never a bucket, a storage key or a connection. A made file is kept as long as the pipeline keeps its run's files (expiresAt); after that it is listed as expired and its download is 410.

operationId: getRunOutputs

item.name: A completed run's answer: its final output's rows, masked, at most 100 rows and 16 KB -- or the run's report as PDF, HTML or Markdown.

header.description: Without format: application/json, application/pdf, text/html or text/markdown (by q, then order; */* is json). An Accept naming none of them is a 400 (unsupported-format). For POST /pipelines/{pipelineId}/runs only with wait.

query.description: json (the default), pdf, html or md. Wins over Accept. Anything else is a 400 (unsupported-format).
pdf, html and md of a run that made several reports: which one, by its number (RPT-0093).

request.description:
A completed run's answer: its final output's rows, masked, at most 100 rows and 16 KB -- or the run's report as PDF, HTML or Markdown.

The rows of the last step of the run's latest attempt that kept an output, as the pipeline's own data -- the answer a run-and-wait gives when the run ends in time. Every column the workspace's data policy marks sensitive (the Data Catalog's sensitive assets, and a person's details in a pipeline marked sensitive) is masked, and named in `masked`; at most 100 rows and 16 KB of JSON (`truncated` says when there were more). An output past the pipeline's retention, or a run that kept none, answers no rows and says why in `problem`. A run that has not completed is a 409 (`run-not-completed`); another workspace's run a 404. The format is the client's choice -- `format` (json, pdf, html, md), or the Accept header (application/json, application/pdf, text/html, text/markdown; a wildcard is json); json when neither says, and any other format is a 400 (`unsupported-format`) naming the allowed ones. pdf, html and md are the run's report (its Generate report step): its PDF -- the signed one once approved and signed --, its HTML, or Markdown made from that HTML (headings, tables and lists; pictures, signatures, charts and the QR code as links to the PDF), whose first line names it ("From signed report RPT-0093 version 1") -- Markdown is never signed: the PDF is the record. A run that made several reports (one per row) names one with `report` (else 409 `several-reports`, listing them in `reports`). Without a report, html and md are the result rows above as a table (masked the same way), and pdf is a 404 (`no-report`). A pipeline marked sensitive keeps its report from API clients in every format (403 `sensitive-files`), as its files; a report made without the format's source (a PDF-only report has no HTML, so no Markdown) is a 404 (`format-not-kept`); one whose files the workspace's retention removed is a 410 (`report-expired`). A document's answer says what it is made from in X-Result-Source (report or rows) and, for a report, X-Report, X-Report-Version and X-Report-Signed; it is never cached (Cache-Control: no-store) and comes as an attachment.

operationId: getRunResult

item.name: The run's items: each file, recording, document or row it processed one by one, with its status.

query.description: failed takes in an item with failed sub-items.

request.description:
The run's items: each file, recording, document or row it processed one by one, with its status.

A pipeline that works item by item (a step per recording, per file, per document, per row of a per-row call, or one that splits a PDF into its pages) keeps one item per thing it processed: its status (running, done, failed), the step it failed at and why in words, how many of its sub-items (a document's pages) failed, and the files its steps made for it, by file id (GET /v1/files/{fileId} downloads one). In the run's order, cursor paging; parentId lists one item's sub-items. Any other run -- one that reads a table whole -- has no items: an empty list. An item retried in a later attempt shows its latest version (attempt). Never a bucket, a key in a bucket or a storage key.

operationId: listRunItems

item.name: One item of a run, with each of its steps.

request.description:
One item of a run, with each of its steps.

The item by its id ("2"; a sub-item "3.12") -- or by its key, when the key has no '/'. As listRunItems lists it, with steps: each step's status for this item (done, failed, not_run, shared -- a combining step whose output belongs to many items, sharedBy saying how many -- or left_out, when a filter left the item out), its message, rows and files.

operationId: getRunItem

item.name: A signed, read-only link to the run's page (15 minutes) to embed in a portal.

request.description:
A signed, read-only link to the run's page (15 minutes) to embed in a portal.

A link to the console's page /embed/runs/{token}: the run's status and times, its steps, the files it made (each with a download) and its review, read-only, with no console navigation and no sign-in. Open it on its own or show it in an iframe: only the origins the API client's frame allow-list names may frame it (Developers › API Clients; the page answers Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors with them, 'none' when there are none), and it refuses everything once it has expired. Append `?theme=light` or `dark`, and `accent=<hex colour>` (e.g. 0b6bcb), to fit the portal. The link opens that one run only: no other run, no file it does not list, nothing of the API. A revoked client's links end at once. Nothing is stored and nothing is billed but this call, so no Idempotency-Key: each call answers a new link. Give each visitor a fresh link rather than a long-lived one.

operationId: createViewLink

item.name: What a view link's page shows, through the link's own token.

variable.description: The token of a view link's URL.

request.description:
What a view link's page shows, through the link's own token.

No access token: the view link's token is the permission, for that one run, read-only, until it expires. The console's page reads this; a portal's server may too. Times are UTC. Each file the run made carries a download (a signed file link, GET /v1/files/{fileId}/content) that ends no later than the view. refreshSeconds says when a run that is still moving is worth reading again (null once it has settled). Not counted as an API call and not billed: a signed link is free, and only POST view-links is. 410 once expired (`/problems/link-expired`) or when the client that made it was revoked or has expired (`/problems/link-ended`); 404 for a token this API did not make.

operationId: readRunView

item.name: Who may frame a view link's page -- the console's server asks before serving it.

variable.description: The token of a view link's URL.

request.description:
Who may frame a view link's page -- the console's server asks before serving it.

The origins the API client's frame allow-list names, also as the `Embed-Frame-Ancestors` header (a CSP source list, `'none'` when the list is empty), which the console's server sends as Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors with the page. An expired link still answers its origins (state `expired`), so the portal shows that it expired rather than a broken frame; its data is refused. 404, and frame-ancestors 'none', for a token this API did not make or a revoked client's.

operationId: readRunViewFrame

item.name: backfills
item.description: Running a pipeline once for each day, hour or week of a past range.

item.name: Run a pipeline once for each day (hour, week) of a past range, a few at a time.

request.description:
Run a pipeline once for each day (hour, week) of a past range, a few at a time.

Makes a backfill: one run of the pipeline for each period of `from`..`to` (both days included), counted in the workspace's billing time zone (America/Chicago unless set) -- a day is midnight to midnight there, so 23 or 25 hours on a daylight-saving day; an hour is a clock hour; a week is seven days from each start day. Each run's steps read `{{run.date}}` (the period's day), `{{run.windowStart}}` and `{{run.windowEnd}}` (its bounds, RFC 3339 with the zone's offset) and every `{{param.name}}` of `parameters`. At most 366 periods, and nothing that has not begun yet. A period that already has a completed run of the pipeline (a scheduled run whose slot falls in it, or an earlier backfill's) is skipped unless `rerunCompleted` is true. Answered once the backfill is made; its runs are queued gradually, at most `concurrency` at a time (1 to 4, as the platform's memory budget allows), beside the pipeline's own runs, and each is billed as any run. Refused (409, the problem's `type` says why) when the workspace already has 3 open backfills (`too-many-backfills`), a period is in another open backfill of the pipeline (`backfill-overlaps`), every period already has a completed run (`nothing-to-run`), the pipeline is inactive (`pipeline-inactive`) or has no steps (`pipeline-not-backfillable`); 422 (`invalid-parameters`) when a value does not suit its parameter.

operationId: startBackfill

item.name: A backfill, its progress and its periods.

request.description:
A backfill, its progress and its periods.

The backfill's status (`running`, `paused`, `cancelled`, `completed` -- every period completed or skipped --, or `failed` -- at least one period failed), how many periods are in each state, why it waits when it does (`waitingReason`: the workspace is suspended, the pipeline is switched off), when it should end, and its first 100 periods with each one's run (follow a run as any run, `GET /runs/{runId}`). A failed period keeps its run's last message as `note`.

operationId: getBackfill

item.name: Cancel a backfill.

request.description:
Cancel a backfill.

Nothing more is queued: its waiting periods are cancelled. The runs already started finish and are recorded on their periods. Refused (409 `backfill-closed`) when the backfill has ended already.

operationId: cancelBackfill

item.name: files
Upload a file for a run or a form; answers its file id.

request.description:
Upload a file for a run or a form; answers its file id.

Stored in the workspace's inbox (role input) and named by a ULID, the only id of a file a customer sees; nothing starts because of an upload. Its size is limited by the workspace (413), its kind is checked against its content (422). 409 when the workspace has no inbox yet, or for an Idempotency-Key reused with another file.

operationId: uploadFile

item.name: Redirects to a signed link valid 5 minutes.

request.description:
Redirects to a signed link valid 5 minutes.

A file of the workspace's -- one it uploaded, or one a run made (the manifest's) -- answered with a 302 to its signed link on this API (/v1/files/{fileId}/content?token=...), valid 5 minutes. The link needs no token, so a portal may hand it to a browser; it opens that one file only, and never names a bucket or a storage key. The body says the same for a caller that does not follow redirects. A made file past its expiry is 410. A file a pipeline marked sensitive made (a saved file, a report's PDF) is the pipeline's real output, never masked: an API client is refused it with a 403 of type sensitive-files until a scope for it is offered -- its meta still describes it.

operationId: downloadFile

item.name: The file's bytes, through the signed link GET /v1/files/{fileId} answered.

request.description:
The file's bytes, through the signed link GET /v1/files/{fileId} answered.

No access token: the link's signature is the permission, for this file only, until it expires (5 minutes). A link that has expired is 410 (ask GET /v1/files/{fileId} for a new one); a link that is not one this API made, or names another file, is 404. A file a pipeline marked sensitive made is 403 (sensitive-files), as GET /v1/files/{fileId}.

operationId: readFileContent

item.name: A file's facts: name, size, sha256, role.

request.description:
A file's facts: name, size, sha256, role.

operationId: getFile

item.name: reviews
item.description: The customer's decision on a run's results.

item.name: The run's review: who must decide and what they decided.

request.description:
The run's review: who must decide and what they decided.

operationId: getReview

item.name: The customer's decision on a completed run (the CUSTOMER party).

request.description:
The customer's decision on a completed run (the CUSTOMER party).

The same rules as the console's review: the run is completed, its pipeline asks for a customer review (settings.review.required), the run's results are still pending, and the customer has not decided yet -- otherwise 409. A rejection says why (reason); rerun asks for the pipeline to run again as a new run, which only a run started through the API can be (it is started again with the same intake); a re-run that cannot start leaves the rejection standing and says why in rerun.message. Sending the same Idempotency-Key again returns the first answer.

operationId: decideReview

item.name: events
item.description: Events in, and the catalogue of events out.

item.name: An event from the organisation's systems; the workspace's event routes start what it names.

request.description:
An event from the organisation's systems; the workspace's event routes start what it names.

The type is the organisation's own; the workspace's event routes (set in the console) say which pipeline or workflow it starts, and may name a data contract the data must meet (422 with each field's path under "data", nothing started). A type no route takes is 422 at "type". Each route's pipeline gets a run with the data as its record; each workflow route a request whose subject is the event. What could not start is in notStarted, with why (a run of that pipeline still in flight, say).

operationId: sendEvent

item.name: The catalogue of event types the platform sends (each with its JSON Schema).

request.description:
The catalogue of event types the platform sends (each with its JSON Schema).

A registry, not a fixed list: a new event type appears here, and becomes subscribable, when the platform adds it. Each entry's schema is the JSON Schema of the event's data, self-contained.

operationId: listEventTypes

item.name: webhooks
The webhook subscriptions.

request.description:
The webhook subscriptions.

operationId: listWebhooks

item.name: Subscribe a URL to event types; the signing secret is shown once.

request.description:
Subscribe a URL to event types; the signing secret is shown once.

The URL must be https and every address its host resolves to public: a private, loopback, link-local or metadata address is refused here (422 at url), and again at every delivery. A workspace has at most 20 webhooks (409). Only events that happen after the webhook is made are sent to it. In a workspace our team manages, webhooks are set up by our team: making, changing, removing and rotating are 403 there.

operationId: createWebhook

item.name: One subscription.

request.description:
One subscription.

operationId: getWebhook

item.name: Change the URL, the event types, or pause it.

request.description:
Change the URL, the event types, or pause it.

active false pauses the webhook: nothing more is sent to it, and what was still waiting is marked failed. active true resumes it (and clears a pause the platform made after repeated failures); only events after that are sent.

operationId: updateWebhook

item.name: Remove a subscription; nothing more is sent to it.

request.description:
Remove a subscription; nothing more is sent to it.

operationId: deleteWebhook

item.name: A new secret; the old one is accepted alongside it for 24 hours.

request.description:
A new secret; the old one is accepted alongside it for 24 hours.

operationId: rotateWebhookSecret

item.name: A subscription's delivery attempts, newest first.

request.description:
A subscription's delivery attempts, newest first.

item.name: Send a delivery again.

request.description:
Send a delivery again.

A new delivery of the same event (the same Webhook-Id), sent within seconds and retried like any other; it names the delivery it repeats. The webhook must be active (409 when paused), and the event still kept.

operationId: redeliver
